answer: A grading network plants honeypot answers—deliberately flawed submissions with unique pigment, a signature only the system knows. When colluding graders award high scores to these traps, the dawn of their coordination becomes visible: identical false positives ripple across their history. Each fake identity an attacker spins up must either grade honestly, losing its value as a sybil, or collude and trigger the trap. The cost scales with volume—more identities mean more chances to stumble into honeypots, and once one sybil is caught, graph analysis exposes the cluster.
